title: Enrollment, Term Length and Waiting Period of a Rental Property Service Contract
content:
**1. Property covered.** A Rental Property Service Contracts contract covers a residential property the landlord rents out or holds for rent. Single-unit tiers cover one dwelling unit; multi-unit tiers cover every unit of a two- to four-unit building under one contract.

**2. Entry gate.** The property type, unit count and year built are taken from the landlord's statement and must satisfy the entry gate of the tier purchased. These facts rest on what the landlord states for the property address being enrolled, before the enrollment.

**3. Term.** Each term lasts the tier's term length in calendar months (12 months on every tier), ending on the day before the same calendar day that many months later, or on the last day of the month when that day does not exist.

**4. Coverage effective date.** The coverage effective date is the start date plus the tier's waiting period in calendar days (30 days on every tier).

**5. Activation.** The contract activates no earlier than the tier's waiting period in calendar days after the contract is purchased, counting the purchase date as day zero. The purchase date is the start date recorded on the contract; activation on the boundary day itself is allowed.

**6. Tenant contact.** The landlord may name one authorized tenant contact on the contract.

## Clause 5 on the calendar (30-day waiting period)

| Day counted from the purchase date | Activation |
|---|---|
| Day 0 (the purchase date) | not yet |
| Day 29 | not yet |
| Day 30 | allowed: the earliest day |
| Day 31 or later | allowed |

*Hypothetical:* a contract purchased on 10 March has a coverage effective date of 9 April (10 March plus 30 calendar days) and may activate from 9 April; on 8 April it is still in its waiting period. Its first term ends on 9 March of the following year.

## Clause 2 points of judgement

- The landlord's statement is the source for property type, unit count and year built.
- A one-unit condominium stated by the landlord fits a single-unit tier; a stated three-unit building fits only a multi-unit tier.
